publishedExpectations.claim: Interviews focus on collaborative problem solving: 'asking great questions is more important than knowing all the answers', and the firm considers applicants for every open role, not just the one applied to.
Quantitative Trading interviews will not test knowledge of finance or economics; they assess how you work with others to solve problems.
Jane Street publishes a Probability & Markets Guide (PDF) covering core concepts that may be encountered in trading interviews.
Technology candidates work through coding challenges during interviews and should be comfortable with their own tools of choice.
Machine Learning candidates interview on realistic modeling problems of the kind the team does daily, at market scale.
FAQ: no GPA or degree requirement, no cover letter required, no finance background needed, and applicants from many universities and concentrations are interviewed.

notes: Jane Street's own interviewing page is unusually explicit and is the primary source here: collaborative problem solving over memorised answers, no finance-knowledge testing for trading, coding challenges for technology, and a published Probability & Markets Guide. Community-reported patterns (unverified): multiple rounds of probability puzzles, mental math under time pressure, and markets/estimation games, plus coding interviews in OCaml-adjacent style; treat the specifics as unconfirmed since they do not appear on official pages. Sourced FAQ facts worth acting on: no GPA cut-off, no cover letter, and applications are considered across all open roles. The strongest verifiable prep signal is deep probability and expected-value reasoning, which the firm itself endorses via its published guide.
